lessons.diagnosis: HIT. Hormuz transits stayed far below half of pre-war on every reading in the window. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 a day (about 5 percent); Kpler's separate commodity-vessel count ran 7 to 20+ a day and its 10/8 report called transits the lowest in over two months; later reports on 10/21 put crossings at 4-5 a day. No tracker came near 50 percent. The 9/22 'may reopen within 7 days' report that motivated the row did NOT convert - transits fell, tanker attacks hit a record week (week before 10/8), and a supertanker hit a mine on 10/17. That is the fifth reopening signal in this war with no durable reopening.
lessons.patch: none - variance is not the right word either: this is the 'physical flow lags the headline' mechanism (13g) working as priced. CAVEAT recorded for the scorer: the row named no resolution source ('published weekly laden-tanker transits'); trackers count different vessel classes and disagree on baselines, so it was scored on PortWatch (all ships, baseline 85) with Kpler as corroboration. Manual rows should name the series at logging (schema R30 does for analyst rows; ledger.py add does not).
